title: Which fraction gives the length of this blue line?
description: A number line from zero to two has each unit cut into three equal parts, and a blue line runs from zero to the second mark. The board finds the size of one part, counts the parts under the blue line and multiplies. Keeko doubts the count by including the mark at zero.
teaching_notes: One idea: a length is the number of parts it covers times the size of one part. Watch for students who count the mark at zero as a part.

source: On a number line from 0 to 2, each unit is divided into thre
video_script.why: A learner writes a length covering more than one part as a count of parts times the size of one part.
video_script.substitution: the book's own number line with each unit cut into three equal parts
video_script.anchor: the number line from 0 to 2 with each unit cut into three equal parts and a blue line from 0 to the second mark
video_script.wrong_answer: three thirds, because it touches three marks
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the mark at zero as well, so the blue line seems to touch three marks and to be three parts long.
video_script.payoff_line: The blue line is two thirds of a unit long

final_answer.spoken: the blue line is two thirds of a unit long

video_script.fraction_reading: one third, two thirds, three fourths
never_show: 3/3 as the length of the blue line
maths_rules: 1 unit cut into 3 equal parts: each part is 1/3 unit
the blue line covers 2 parts, from 0 to the second mark
check: 3 x 1/3 = 1 unit, and the blue line is shorter than 1 unit
video_script.design: The same number line, now with three parts in each unit. The blue line covers two parts, and Keeko's doubt counts the mark at zero.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a number line from 0 to 2; each unit cut into three equal parts; the first mark labelled 1/3; a blue line from 0 to the second mark

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.line: the number line from 0 to 2 appears with each unit cut into three equal parts
marks.blue: a blue line runs from 0 to the second mark

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it uses a number line.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Each unit is cut into three equal parts, and the first mark is labelled one third.
<bookmark mark='blue'/>A blue line goes from zero to the second mark.
Which fraction gives the length of the blue line?

beats.on_screen: the number line and the blue line stay; the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the three equal parts of the first unit in three shades; a strip of three fourths split as 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4

marks.parts: the three parts of the first unit get three shades
marks.read: a strip of three fourths is shown as three copies of one fourth

beats.colours: three shades for the three parts
narration: <bookmark mark='parts'/>The three equal parts of a unit are called thirds.
<bookmark mark='read'/>A fraction can be read as a count of parts.
Three fourths is three times one fourth.

beats.on_screen: Given: each unit is cut into 3 equal parts
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, each unit is cut into three equal parts, and the blue line ends at the second mark.

beats.on_screen: To find: the fraction for the length of the blue line
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the fraction that gives the length of the blue line.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 1 unit into 3 equal parts, each part = 1/3

marks.size: one part is lit and labelled 1/3

narration: <bookmark mark='size'/>Step one, find the size of each part. One unit cut into three equal parts gives one third each.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: parts under the blue line = 2

marks.count: the blue line is traced and the parts are counted one, two

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step two, count the parts under the blue line. It stops at the second mark, so it covers two parts.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: length = number of parts x size of one part = 2 x 1/3

marks.times: the count and the size are joined with a times sign

narration: <bookmark mark='times'/>Step three, multiply the number of parts by the size of one part. That is two times one third.

beats.on_screen: Check: 3 x 1/3 = 1 unit, and the blue line covers fewer parts

marks.check: the third part is shaded to reach 1; the blue line stops short of it

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, three parts of one third make one unit. The blue line has fewer parts, so it is shorter than one.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Two times one third is two thirds. The blue line is two thirds of a unit long.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says 3 parts because 3 marks are touched; the mark at 0 is circled and crossed out; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.zero: the mark at 0 is circled and crossed out
marks.fix: the two parts light up one after the other

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the blue line is three thirds, because it touches three marks.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>But zero is only where we start. It does not cover any part.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The blue line covers two parts, so we count parts and not marks.
